title: Thermal behavior in FeCuCrCoNi high entropy alloy nanoparticles: an atomistic approach.

recollection.starting_material: Equimolar Fe–Cu–Cr–Co–Ni high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (5–10 nm diameter) prepared as ideal random solid‐solution seeds
recollection.intervention: Classical molecular‐dynamics simulations (EAM potentials) with stepwise heating from 300 K to 1800 K under NPT conditions
recollection.structure: Initially single‐phase fcc random solid solution; upon heating, progressive surface segregation of Cu and Ni forming a Cu–Ni–rich shell and a Cr–Co–Fe–rich core
recollection.mechanism: Surface‐energy driven atomic diffusion and preferential segregation of the lowest‐energy species (Cu, Ni) to the surface; surface premelting initiates at undercoordinated sites and propagates inward
recollection.results: Surface premelting onset around 900 K, partial melting at ∼1100 K, complete nanoparticle melting by ∼1500 K; activation energy for atomic diffusion ~0.5 eV; at 1200 K, surface Cu enrichment reaches ~60 at% (core drops to ~20 at%)

score.note: The recollection correctly identifies classical MD with an EAM potential, heating from 300 K, and an initially random equiatomic FCC nanoparticle, but gives inaccurate size/temperature and ensemble details. Its proposed Cu–Ni shell, core–shell segregation, and inward-propagating surface-premelting mechanism contradict the paper, which found no stable segregation or substantial liquid shell and emphasized element-specific Fe/Cu mobility from both surface and core. The reported melting temperatures, diffusion activation energy, and Cu enrichment are unsupported; it also misses the inverse-radius fit (c = -0.978) and fitted bulk melting point of 2184 K.
